steps.step: Send Doug a one-paragraph note on the consent-flag filter at ingestion, written so his privacy team can review it. (owner Nia Oduya, due 2026-10-02). Why: Doug downplayed it as 'could be nothing' but said it might kill attribution; AEs tend to treat casual asides as noise.

judge.critique: Strong step: it turns Doug's offhand privacy worry into a dated, SC-owned note the privacy team can review; the weakest point is that it should state plainly that whether the join is allowed is the privacy team's call (per U044) and avoid implying Apex can resolve it.

steps.step: Ask Doug by email what outcome Ann cares about in his words, and whether Ann signs, before the Oct 7 one pager. (owner Ryan Castellano, due 2026-10-05). Why: CRM shows outcome prefilled from discovery, not said on the call, and nobody said Ann signs; easy to assume both.

judge.critique: Weakest is R3: the email only gathers information for Ryan and gives Doug nothing to forward to Ann, so pair the question with a draft outline of the one pager for Doug to react to.
